It provides a stable baseload for electricity grids, especially in regions where renewable energy infrastructure is underdeveloped or inconsistent. Unlike solar or wind, coal plants operate continuously, ensuring power during peak demand or adverse weather. Many countries, particularly in Asia, rely heavily on coal for industrial processes like steel and cement production, where alternatives are costly or technologically immature. In 2023, coal supplied about 20% of global electricity, with demand projected to remain steady through 2030 due to energy security needs. While renewables are growing, their intermittency and high transition costs make coal's role hard to replace in the short term, especially in developing economies. #coal #mining …...more ...more Show less How this was madeAuto-dubbedAudio tracks for some languages were automatically generated.
